text:
jordan: Quick q — planning a Terraform change to add a short-burst capacity tier to the gpu-nodepool for inference-burst workloads. Goal: keep 2 guaranteed on-demand nodes (reserved capacity) and allow autoscale up to 20 using spot instances. Main asks: recommended instance mix, taints/labels for scheduling, and where to wire the kube secrets (Vault vs SOPS). PR WIP: https://git.redwood.dev/r/redwood/infra/pull/432

mira: SG. A few quick points — prefer mixing within the same family to avoid perf variance (e.g., h100-48/h100-80 if available) rather than mixing p4 + h100. For TF, this pattern has worked for us:

```hcl
module "gpu_nodepool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@git.redwood.dev/infra/modules//eks-node-group"
  name   = "gpu-burst"
  desired_capacity = 2
  max_capacity     = 20
  instance_types   = ["h100.48x", "h100.80x"]
  spot_percentage  = 80
  taints = { "redwood/gpu": "true:NoSchedule" }
}
```

Also add a node label like `node.k8s.redwood/pool=gpu-burst` so schedulers and cost tooling can pick it up. For scheduling, add a toleration in the inference deployment: `key: redwood/gpu, operator: Equal, value: "true", effect: NoSchedule`

samir: A couple infra cautions: if you rely on spot for most capacity, add a fallback policy so the autoscaler can scale into on-demand if spot is constrained — we do that via an `instance_family_preference` and a small on-demand reserve. For reservation on AWS we used the `aws_ec2_capacity_reservation` resource in the past for the 2 guaranteed nodes. Example snippet: 

```hcl
resource "aws_ec2_capacity_reservation" "gpu_reserved" {
  instance_type = "h100.48x"
  availability_zone = "us-west-2a"
  instance_count = 2
  tags = { Name = "gpu-burst-reserve" }
}
```

On the secret wiring: prefer Vault for private keys/configs. Put the kubeconfig/credentials at `secret/data/infra/gpu-nodepool/kubecreds` and sync into the k8s cluster using the vault-agent sidecar or the cluster-k8s-secret-syncer. If you must check into TF, encrypt with SOPS and never store plaintext.

laura: One more infra ops nit: cluster-autoscaler annotations we use for this pool: `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=false` on pods that pin to reserved nodes, and annotate the node group with `alpha.eksctl.io/managed=true` so our rollout scripts pick it up. Also ensure the nodegroup's IAM role has the `ec2:CreateFleet` permission if we want dynamic fallback to on-demand.

infra-bot: CI: terraform validate passed, but `tflint` flagged unused var `gpu_types` in modules/eks-node-group/vars.tf. Also running a dry-run plan returned a changed count of +2 capacity and +1 taint change.

jordan: Thanks all — I'll update the PR to: 1) set instance_types to h100 family, 2) add the capacity_reservation resource for the 2 nodes, 3) add the taint/label bits and autoscaler annotations, and 4) wire Vault path `secret/data/infra/gpu-nodepool/kubecreds`. Will ping for review once CI goes green.

mira: One tiny suggestion before merge: add a small terraform `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [taints] }` on the node group if you'll be making runtime changes from ops scripts, otherwise drifts will be noisy.

samir: Ping me on the PR once updated, I can fast-track the review after CI.

laura: If you want I can pre-create the Vault path and give the kube-syncer a token — saves a deploy step.

jordan: Please do, laura. Tag me when done and I'll re-run the plan. :thumbsup:
